solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Time to abandon HGV and dismiss carrier

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped from the lorry word

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
an HGV (heavy goods vehicle) is a lorry or truck
to sack someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.surface: A lorry driver is told to leave the heavy truck behind and lay off the haulage firm.
explanation.walkthrough: HGV is the British term for a heavy goods vehicle, a big lorry; 'carrier' sounds like a haulier but is a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpack is a bag worn on the shoulders for hauling belongings, so it is literally something that carries things.

clue.text: Directions for making dish ready to eat around City

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for ready goes outside the abbreviation

blocks.note: fruit ready to eat is ripe
EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: Instructions for a meal ready to serve in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode letters are the usual crossword abbreviation for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is the set of cooking instructions telling you how to prepare a particular meal.

clue.text: Guerrilla leader overwhelming European port for so long

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the leader and port surround the single letter

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the guerrilla leader
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A rebel commander takes over a European harbour for an extended period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' reads as a length of time but is a farewell. Cheerio is a British way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways of saying goodbye when parting from someone.

clue.text: Underwater crewman’s regular payment, one grabbed by literary miser

indicators.note: something grabbed by another is held within its grip, so the numeral sits inside the miser

blocks.note: a sub is a subscription, a regular payment
Silas Marner, George Eliot's miser
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor's wages, part of which a miserly character in a novel has pocketed.
explanation.walkthrough: Silas Marner is the miserly weaver of George Eliot's 1861 novel; a sub is British for a subscription or membership fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A submariner is a sailor serving aboard a submarine, which travels beneath the sea.

clue.text: Supercilious criminal going down

blocks.note: a con is a convict
descending is going down

explanation.surface: An arrogant crook is sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal going down' suggests a sentence being passed; it is two plain pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A patronising person treats others as inferior, which is the haughty, superior attitude of someone supercilious.

clue.text: Writer crossing key expanse of water

indicators.note: a pen crossing something stretches over it, so the writer's letters sit either side of the key

blocks.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone with a pen is striking through a key passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a door or a map legend, but it is a computer keyboard key; Bic is a well-known ballpoint brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic is the sea lying between Scandinavia and mainland northern Europe, a large body of salt water.

clue.text: Mischievous Mike pulling out of parade

indicators.note: pulling out of something means withdrawing from it, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a march is a parade

explanation.surface: A cheeky man named Mike drops out of a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: MARCH loses its M, leaving ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch look or remark is playfully knowing and teasing, which is impish or cheeky.

clue.text: Capital journey round Long Island

blocks.note: a trip is a journey
O is round in shape
LI is the abbreviation for Long Island

explanation.surface: A tour of Long Island, perhaps to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a container signal but here it gives the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya, on the North African Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Study dance, a former Stock Exchange procedure

blocks.note: to con is an old word for to study
the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: Learning a dance turns out to be an old City trading practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Contango was the charge for deferring settlement of a share purchase on the London market, a long-abandoned arrangement.

clue.text: Long tapering rod with copper point

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A slim pole fitted with a copper tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper point' reads like a metal tip on the rod, but copper and point each give their own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The stick used to strike balls in snooker or billiards narrows steadily from butt to tip.

clue.text: Chap, European, with ginger group, doing good

blocks.note: Ben is a man's name, standing for any chap
E is the abbreviation for European
a ginger group is a pressure group within a party, i.e. a faction

explanation.surface: A man from Europe joins an activist group to do some good.
explanation.walkthrough: A ginger group is a British term for a small group pushing a larger body to act; 'ginger' is not hair colour here.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable giving or a kindly gift is an act of kindness performed for others' benefit.

clue.text: Best possible prediction, but it makes us tense!

definitions.text: Best possible prediction, but it makes us tense!

blocks.note: surface reading: an ideal forecast of things to come
setter's reading: a grammatical tense, such as 'we will have gone'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like anxiety about the future, but it is a grammar term: the form 'will have done'.
explanation.definitionFit: This verb form describes an action that will have been completed by some later time, e.g. 'we will have finished'.

clue.text: Left to hosts the last word in singing technique

indicators.note: whatever hosts something takes it in, so the following words sit inside the earlier ones

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
taken as written
amen is said at the end of a prayer, the final word

explanation.surface: Someone left behind hosts a party where the singing gets the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is the nautical sense, the side of a ship; 'the last word' is the word that closes a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: In vocal music this is a smooth glide from one pitch to the next, a recognised method of vocal delivery.

clue.text: Fellow attorney’s notes at conclusion of work

blocks.note: co- means fellow or joint, as in co-worker
DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A lawyer's colleague jots down notes when a case is wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is' joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a musical piece, the final bars that round off a composition.

clue.text: Support woman torn apart by decade attached to church

indicators.note: something torn apart by another is split open with that thing in the gap

blocks.note: Susan is a woman's name
a decade is ten years
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman's life is wrecked by ten years tied to a church, yet she draws strength from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torn apart' suggests an anagram, but the woman's name is simply split in two with the number in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustenance is food and nourishment that keeps a person going, so it supports life.

clue.text: Set of signs originally observed in parts of Cadiz

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept
to part something is to break it up, so the town's letters are separated and rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letter of observed
the Spanish port, taken as written

explanation.surface: Signs seen on a walk around the Spanish city of Cadiz.
explanation.walkthrough: The O is put among the shuffled letters of CADIZ to give ZODIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is the band of twelve astrological star signs, Aries through Pisces, used in horoscopes.

clue.text: Exciting accommodation for Cockneys by river

indicators.note: Cockney speech famously drops the h at the start of words, so the opening h goes

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
housing is accommodation

explanation.surface: Riverside homes for East Londoners make a thrilling prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class East Londoners whose accent famously drops the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rousing speech or song stirs people up and gets them enthusiastic, which is thrilling.

clue.text: Possible bride’s day at Cornish resort? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter of the place is cut

blocks.note: Newlyn is a fishing port in Cornwall
Wed is short for Wednesday

explanation.surface: A bride's big day at a seaside resort in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Newlyn is a fishing town in Cornwall in south-west England. The apostrophe-s stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride is just one example of someone recently married, so the definition carries a question mark.

clue.text: In French art, a seabird from Asia, perhaps

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so the article goes within the French verb

blocks.note: 'thou art' is 'tu es' in French, so art is es
taken as written
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A painting of a seabird in a French gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' suggests painting, but it is the old verb form 'thou art', rendered in French as 'tu es'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coming from Asia can be described as Oriental, belonging to the East; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: A vehicle principally noted in South Africa’s grasslands

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so only the opening letter of noted is kept
in places those pieces inside the abbreviation for the country

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
taken as written
a van is a vehicle
the first letter of noted

explanation.surface: A truck spotted out on the South African plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Africa's' reads as possessive, but the country's abbreviation wraps the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Savanna is open tropical grassland with scattered trees, typical of much of Africa.

clue.text: Clear case first of investigators dropped

indicators.note: first of points to just the opening letter of the following word
dropped means left out, so that letter is removed from the other word

blocks.note: a doctor's case is a patient
the opening letter of investigators

explanation.surface: A detective agency abandons an obvious case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a police matter, but it is a medical case: PATIENT minus I gives PATENT.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, patent means obvious or plain to see, as in a patent lie.

clue.text: Like a river: nothing to do with the ears

blocks.note: nil means nothing
otic is the medical adjective for the ear

explanation.surface: A flowing river has nothing to do with hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A river' is not any river: the answer means of the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic means relating to the Nile, the great African waterway, so the setter's 'like a river' is cagey.

clue.text: Lad carrying American tool unknown in German state

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so the lad's word goes round the tool

blocks.note: a son is a lad
ax is the American spelling of axe
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A boy hauling a mysterious American implement around Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' signals the US spelling of the tool without its final E; 'unknown' is the algebra convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxony is one of the federal states of Germany, with Dresden as its capital.

clue.text: End of novel this writer’s not previously recorded

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of novel
this writer is the setter, I; this writer's = I have = I'VE

explanation.surface: An author admits the ending of a novel has not been written down before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is a crossword convention for the setter, so 'this writer's' is I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A live broadcast or performance happens in real time rather than being taped earlier.

clue.text: Aromatic oil from metropolis endlessly attracting Reagan and Fitzgerald?

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter of that word is cut

blocks.note: a metropolis is a big city
Ronald Reagan, US president, known as Ron
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer

explanation.surface: A city scent that draws in a president and a jazz singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the names are clued by surnames: Ron Reagan and Ella Fitzgerald.
explanation.definitionFit: Citronella is a lemon-scented essential oil from a grass, used in candles to repel insects.

clue.text: Old monk’s sleeping-place at end of compline

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: a bed is a place to sleep
the final letter of compline

explanation.surface: A monk going to his bed after the last service of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Compline is the last church service of the day, so the surface is a monk turning in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian of the early eighth century.

clue.text: Laying out tenner, I grew a woodland plant

indicators.note: laying things out arranges them afresh, so the letters are set down in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, all eleven letters

explanation.surface: A gardener spends ten pounds and raises a forest plant.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintergreen is a low evergreen shrub of North American forests, source of a minty oil.

clue.text: Chinese philosophy Hogarth regularly encountered, going back

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
going back means travelling the other way, so the chosen letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Hogarth

explanation.surface: An Eastern philosophy that the painter Hogarth came across now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tao is 'the Way', the central principle of Taoism, a philosophical tradition of ancient China.

clue.text: Terrible-sounding US politician’s jewelled headband

indicators.note: sounding points to how words are said, not how they are written

blocks.note: dire means terrible; in a non-rhotic British accent it is said 'dia'
Dem is short for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: An awful American politician wearing a jewelled crown.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent dire loses its R, so dire Dem is said like the word for a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a crown or ornamental band worn on the head as a mark of royalty.

clue.text: Able to extend sentence served by youth leader

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of youth is taken

blocks.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence served
the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A youth worker serving time in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth leader' looks like a scout master; it is the first letter of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic can be pulled longer and spring back, like stretchy fabric.
